chapters.title: Chapter 1: Fundamentals of Trademark and Service Mark Protection Under the Lanham Act
chapters.description: Introduces the statutory framework for federal trademark and service mark protection, the functions of marks, and core distinctiveness concepts relevant to registration and scope of rights.
subtopics: Lanham Act overview and policy goals
Trademarks vs. service marks
Spectrum of distinctiveness: generic, descriptive, suggestive, arbitrary, fanciful
Inherent vs. acquired distinctiveness
Word marks, design marks, and standard character marks
Generic/descriptive components and disclaimers
Identifications of goods/services and Nice classification basics

chapters.title: Chapter 2: USPTO Examination and Pre-Registration Process
chapters.description: Explains how applications are examined and prepared for publication, and the tools and references examiners use that later inform TTAB proceedings.
subtopics: Application bases, including Section 1(b) intent-to-use
Substantive examination and office actions
Dictionary evidence and the Trademark ID Manual
Letters of protest: purpose and effect
Approval for publication and the opposition window
Amendments to identifications and their interpretation

chapters.title: Chapter 3: TTAB Opposition Proceedings
chapters.description: Covers how oppositions are initiated and litigated before the TTAB, who may oppose, the burdens of proof, and the evidentiary record.
subtopics: Grounds for opposition, including Lanham Act § 2(d)
Entitlement to bring an opposition (standing-equivalent)
Burden of proof and production; preponderance standard
Pleadings, discovery, trial periods, and briefing
Evidence admissibility and building the record
Use of third-party registrations, marketplace evidence, and internet materials
Board decision structure and remedies

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Federal Circuit Review of TTAB Decisions
chapters.description: Details appellate routes from TTAB decisions, Federal Circuit jurisdiction, and standards of review governing legal conclusions and factual findings.
subtopics: Appeal options: 15 U.S.C. § 1071(a) (Federal Circuit) vs. § 1071(b) (civil action)
Jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1295(a)(4)(B)
Standards of review: de novo for legal questions; substantial-evidence review for factual findings
Definition of substantial evidence and record-based review
Appellate dispositions: affirm, reverse, vacate, remand; partial dispositions

chapters.title: Chapter 5: The DuPont Likelihood-of-Confusion Framework
chapters.description: Provides a comprehensive overview of the multi-factor, flexible analysis used to determine likelihood of confusion under § 2(d).
subtopics: Purpose and structure of the thirteen DuPont factors
Factor interdependence and relative weighting
Factors commonly considered in service-mark cases
No requirement to consider every factor; focus on those of record
Consumer perception as the touchstone

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Factor 2—Relatedness of Goods/Services, Trade Channels, and Purchasers
chapters.description: Explores how tribunals assess whether goods/services are related and how channels of trade and consumer classes affect the analysis.
subtopics: Using identifications as controlling over real-world use
Legal identity “in part” and its presumptions
Inferring trade channels and purchaser overlap from identifications
Role of third-party registrations to show goods/services commonly emanate from a single source
Dictionary and industry evidence to construe service identifications
Financial services context: banking, credit, and financing offerings

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Factor 6—Mark Strength, Third-Party Use, and the Crowded-Field Doctrine
chapters.description: Analyzes how conceptual and commercial strength are established and how third-party use/registration evidence affects the scope of protection.
subtopics: Conceptual vs. commercial strength; inherent distinctiveness and marketplace recognition
Relevance of third-party use and registrations on similar goods/services
Quantitative and qualitative assessment of crowding; no rigid numeric thresholds
Effect of crowded fields on consumer discrimination and scope of protection
Similar versus identical goods/services under factor 6
Consistency of the similarity scope across DuPont factors

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Factor 1—Comparing Marks: Appearance, Sound, Connotation, and Commercial Impression
chapters.description: Covers how marks are compared in their entireties and how components contribute to overall commercial impression.
subtopics: Whole-mark comparison and dominant elements
Weight accorded to generic or descriptive matter (e.g., industry terms like “BANK”)
Standard character vs. stylized/design marks and their scope
Connotation and suggestiveness in financial services terminology
Interaction between mark strength (factor 6) and commercial impression (factor 1)

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Evidence Before the TTAB: Types, Sources, and Weight
chapters.description: Describes common evidentiary materials in TTAB cases and how the Board evaluates their probative value.
subtopics: Third-party registrations vs. marketplace use evidence
Internet printouts, business websites, and social media
Dictionary definitions and industry glossaries
USPTO references: TESS/TSDR, Trademark ID Manual, TMEP
Official notice, authentication, and hearsay considerations
Limitations of registrations alone for commercial strength

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Priority, Presumptions, and Registration Doctrines
chapters.description: Explains how priority and statutory presumptions operate in inter partes disputes and how they shape the likelihood-of-confusion inquiry.
subtopics: Priority based on use and filing; constructive use
Section 7(b) presumptions from registrations
Standard character mark scope across depictions
Incontestability basics and limits (conceptual overview)
Tacking and its narrow application (overview)

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Landmark Case—In re E.I. du Pont de Nemours & Co.
chapters.description: Details the seminal decision establishing the thirteen-factor test for likelihood of confusion and its flexible, evidence-driven application.
subtopics: Origins and rationale of the DuPont factors
Balancing approach and factor interdependence
How courts select and weigh relevant factors
Enduring influence on TTAB and Federal Circuit analysis

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Landmark Cases—Crowded Fields and Relatedness of Goods/Services
chapters.description: Synthesizes key precedents that shape factor 2 and factor 6 analyses, including the evidentiary role of third-party uses/registrations and the definition of similarity.
subtopics: Juice Generation: considerable third-party use and reduced mark strength
Jack Wolfskin: voluminous third-party evidence and narrowed protection
Palm Bay Imports: third-party use signaling weaker marks
Coach Services: using third-party registrations to show relatedness and common source
Olde Tyme Foods: similar (not identical) goods/services suffice in the analysis
